Documentation.name: ArchiMate
Documentation.notes: Enterprise architecture modeling using the ArchiMate language.
Documentation.trademark: ArchiMate is a registered trademark of The Open Group.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Meaning
Stereotype.notes: A meaning is the knowledge or expertise present in the representation of a business object, given a particular context.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Value
Stereotype.notes: The value of a product or service is that which makes some party appreciate it, possibly in relation to providing it, but more typically to acquiring it.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Product
Stereotype.notes: A coherent collection of services, accompanied by a contract/set of agreements, which is offered as a whole to (internal or external) customers.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Object
Stereotype.notes: An object is a unit of information.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Representation
Stereotype.notes: A representation is the perceptible form of the information carried by a business object.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Artifact
Stereotype.notes: An artifact is a physical piece of information that is used or produced in a software development process, or by deployment and operation of a system.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Process
Stereotype.notes: A process is a unit of internal behaviour or collection of causally related units of internal behaviour intended to produce a defined set of products and services.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Function
Stereotype.notes: A function represents a coherent group of internal behaviour of a component.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Interaction
Stereotype.notes: An interaction is a unit of behaviour performed as a collaboration of two or more roles.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Service
Stereotype.notes: A service is an externally visible unit of functionality, provided by one or more components, exposed through well-defined interfaces, and meaningful to the environment.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Event
Stereotype.notes: An event is something that happens (internally or externally) and influences behaviour.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Actor
Stereotype.notes: An actor represents an organisational entity that is capable of performing behaviour.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Role
Stereotype.notes: A role is a named specific behaviour of an actor participating in a particular context.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Collaboration
Stereotype.notes: A collaboration defines a (temporary) configuration of two or more components that cooperate to jointly perform application interactions.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Interface
Stereotype.notes: An interface declares how an entity can connect with its environment.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Component
Stereotype.notes: A component is a modular, deployable, and replaceable part of a system that encapsulates its contents and exposes its functionality through a set of interfaces.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Node
Stereotype.notes: A node is a computational resource upon which artifacts may be deployed for execution.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Device
Stereotype.notes: A device is a physical computational resource upon which artifacts may be deployed for execution.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Specialisation
Stereotype.notes: The specialization relationship indicates that an object is a specialization of another object.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Aggregation
Stereotype.notes: The aggregation relationship indicates that a concept groups a number of other concepts.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Assignment
Stereotype.notes: The assignment relationship links units of behaviour with active elements (e.g. roles, components) that perform them, or roles with actors that fulfil them.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Association
Stereotype.notes: An association models a relationship between objects that is not covered by another, more specific relationship.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Realisation
Stereotype.notes: The realization relationship links a logical entity with a more concrete entity that realises it.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Flow
Stereotype.notes: The flow relationship describes the exchange or transfer of, e.g., information or value between processes, function, interactions and events.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_UsedBy
Stereotype.notes: The used by relationship models the use of services by processes, functions or interactions and the access to interfaces by roles, components or collaborations.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Access
Stereotype.notes: The access relationship models the access of behavioural concepts to business or data objects.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_CommunicationPath
Stereotype.notes: A communication path is a relation between two or more nodes, through which these nodes can exchange information.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Junction
Stereotype.notes: A junction is used to connect relationships of the same type.

Stereotype.name: ArchiMate_Grouping
Stereotype.notes: The grouping relationship indicates that objects belong together based on some common characteristic.
